garden-walk:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: immersive future-world visual for an illustrated worldbook.
Primary request: A beautifully plausible future garden neighborhood seen from human eye height while walking through it, landscape 1536x1024, 3:2. Make the viewer feel physically present in a society where autonomous maintenance and shared productive infrastructure let residents inhabit generous landscapes.
Scene: A continuous broad smooth accessible path curves gently along terraced planted water gardens underneath a lush living canopy. One natural human hand rests on a cool pale stone balustrade in the very near foreground. Midground friends are playing with the water near a shallow rill, one older person sits resting, other ordinary neighbors stroll with a wheelchair user. In deep perspective are substantial stepped light-steel and timber dwellings with exposed reusable bolted structural joints, deep shaded balconies, planted roofs and water gardens spanning the neighborhood. The technology feels quiet but real: a compact autonomous gardening machine works behind a low planted work boundary, an unobtrusive low service hatch, sun shading and an integrated slender transit connection in the far distance.
Style: exceptionally crafted realistic architectural concept photography, warm humid morning after light rain, textured surfaces, dappled daylight, rich planting with variety, lived-in inhabitants not posed. Strong sense of depth, foreground touch, middle-ground social life, expansive inhabited garden infrastructure beyond.
Constraints: No letters, labels, logos, numerals, captions or watermark. Not a medieval courtyard or rustic village. Show an advanced legible built environment integrated with nature and water. Not luxury real-estate advertising; no enormous empty atrium. Anatomically natural hand and people. Garden water is landscape water, no claim of drinking-water production. The path remains continuous and easy to use.
garden-section:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: explanatory architectural cutaway concept image for an illustrated worldbook.
Primary request: A large clear continuous architectural section-perspective through an inhabited future garden residential terrace and its material/service level below, landscape 1536x1024, 3:2. Make the reader actually see the engineered systems supporting a generous daily life, with beautiful spatial coherence rather than an abstract diagram.
Composition: Isometric oblique section drawing rendered with photographic material richness, one continuous coherent building and its ground cut open toward the viewer. Upper half: three gently stepped residential levels with exposed pale reusable bolted steel frames, sun shades, openable windows, warm interiors, deep planted balconies, a wide accessible garden path across the front, people resting and sharing food, small cleaning robot on the public route. Show realistic soil depth for the planting. Lower half: a well-lit accessible service corridor below the public path, separate clean and dirty receiving counters in a shared cup-return/washing hub with visible dishwasher enclosure and storage, modular utility trays, a robot-maintenance bay with spare modules and robot carrier route. At one side a cross-section of a planted stormwater root-zone above a rainwater cistern with access hatch; separate clearly legible pipe runs, water does not magically become drinking water. Structure carries loads all the way down with continuous columns and foundations. Atmosphere: light and inviting, humanity above and purposeful machinery below, recoverable components and maintenance access are visible.
Style: sophisticated architectural magazine section-perspective, pale stone, sage foliage, brushed metal, natural timber, muted terracotta, crisp precise sectional edges, large readable spaces, realistic scale and beautiful daylight. It must work without labels.
Constraints: No text, letters, labels, logos, captions, numbers or watermark. No miniature collage, no repeated separate panels, no decorative arrows, no arrows claiming perfect material loops. Not a sealed machine-city: visible maintained systems and material handoffs. The section is a speculative spatial concept, not a certified engineering drawing.
university-cosmos:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: embodied future inquiry scene for an illustrated worldbook.
Primary request: A physically immersive Open University inquiry hall, seen from eye height, where a small intergenerational group joyfully explores astronomical observations through shared room-scale augmented reality. Landscape 1536x1024, 3:2.
Scene: In the very near foreground a participant's natural hands adjust two simple tangible controller rings and an instrument component resting on a real wooden worktable. Across the tactile stone floor are comfortable benches and five companions of different ages, one sitting, one standing in gentle wonder, wearing discreet lightweight clear AR glasses. A magnificent translucent starfield and long elegant flowing orbital tracks share the volume of the lofty hall above them, a comprehensible visualization rather than a physically present galaxy. Some stars and orbital arcs are transparent over the real architecture, visibly showing the viewer the experience through AR glasses. A real telescope instrument sits on an elevated terrace through the open roof, protected by a retractable dome segment; late twilight is visible beyond. The shared simulation feels immense and inviting, with room to walk around and inspect it. A person at a tangible table compares an observed pattern with a visualization. The architecture retains real floors, columns, benches, railings, daylight openings and maintenance doors.
Style: cinematic but candid architectural concept photography, blue twilight and soft amber practical light, believable near-future equipment, subtle elegant interface with no text, tactile foreground, spacious atmosphere. Curiosity, shared wonder and patient understanding rather than an expert delivering a presentation.
Constraints: No letters, numerals, labels, logos, watermark, captions or readable screen text. No auditorium, lectern or corporate slide presentation. No one dominating the scene. The universe is an AR visualization, not matter physically inside the hall. No absurd levitating building elements.
university-workshop:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: lived future public research foundry scene for an illustrated worldbook.
Primary request: A warm, spacious public research foundry within an Open University, seen from visitor eye height, landscape 1536x1024, 3:2. Show how shared knowledge becomes usable instruments through accessible digital design, human curiosity and autonomous fabrication.
Scene: A visitor in the immediate foreground leans lightly at a safe viewing rail, seeing a compact multi-axis robot fabricate and assemble small telescope or optical instrument components behind a clear guard in the left middle ground. Beyond are ordinary shared worktables where two people, one older and one young adult, assemble an optical tube and inspect a lens mount. To the right a public design station has a large screen showing a clear unlabeled 3D exploded view of the instrument and a physical controller. A modular parts library with reusable labeled-by-shape trays and mechanical components lines the wall, with a service robot carrier delivering a tray along a recessed clearly separate service aisle. Glazed courtyard doors at the back reveal people making music and relaxing among trees, so inquiry belongs to a whole inhabited life. Exposed maintainable service carriers, ventilation around guarded fabrication, tidy component return shelves, good natural task light, reusable bolted framing. Show enough machine detail to understand what is happening, without making the image cluttered.
Style: highly convincing architectural concept photography, warm late afternoon daylight, crisp translucent guards, textured wooden tables, pale metal frames, real wear and hands-on tools, diverse ordinary participants, expansive calm and the satisfaction of making something work. Shared abundance rather than industrial employment or private startup culture.
Constraints: No letters, logos, numerals, captions, watermark or readable screen text. No hero founder or person posing, no corporate advertisement, no unsafe open machining next to visitors, no science-fiction reactor. Telescope instrument parts should feel plausible and modest. The foundry is a public place of making, connected to everyday life.
